clinic.text: Clinic: 22 conversions = 15 general-rule + 7 query-specific templates (Q010, Q011, Q012, Q013, Q014, Q016, Q020). 15/22 is code-derived; a separate templates-disabled run has not been measured. Each template is selected by query ID and matches only the exact Clinic source file, so it is not a general conversion rule. Clinic has no author-verified ground truth: pipeline counts, not accuracy.

fee_rainbow.text: Fee-Rainbow: 40 conversions = 39 ground-truth recoverable sites + ambiguous G011; G007 (ambiguous) is not converted. Ground-truth IDs and query IDs differ from G034/Q033 onward (the ground truth also numbers commented-out lines).

dignity_dev.text: Dignity-Dev is the only fresh independent holdout: run untouched, no rule changed for it. Its first holdout run and the current rules give identical S15 results.

ground_truth.text: Ground truth was drafted blind by an LLM and verified by one human (the author). The drafting model is from the same model family as the development assistant, so shared blind spots are possible. Matching is by file and line, never by query ID.

no_overall_score.text: There is deliberately no combined overall accuracy score. Detection, recovery, conversion, column use and behavioural equivalence measure different things.

limitations.title: Branch-dependent SQL
limitations.text: SQL whose text differs between if/else branches is not rebuilt by a general rule. SQL built and executed in the same conditional block is recovered (S13); otherwise C3 abstains with BRANCHING. Only the Clinic templates Q014 and Q016 rebuild branch-dependent SQL, for those exact files.

limitations.title: Column use stops at the SQL statement
limitations.text: Tables and columns read, written and filtered are identified per SQL operation and measured against the ground truth. Use of result columns in later PHP application logic is not traced; that part of FR4 is not implemented.

limitations.title: Unsupported join shapes
limitations.text: The converter accepts static INNER JOIN SELECTs only. Recovered sites with other join forms stay unconverted and are flagged with CONVERSION_UNSUPPORTED.

items.title: SQL Operation Identification
items.requirement: The system must identify database query operations within the legacy PHP source code. This includes 'mysqli', 'mysql', and PDO-based queries.
items.limitation: PDO detection is tested on fixtures only (no third-party benchmark app uses PDO); wrapper detection covers the single-parameter wrapper shape only.

items.title: SQL Recovery
items.requirement: SQL queries constructed using variables, string concatenation, or conditional statements must be reconstructed whenever they can be safely resolved.
items.limitation: SQL whose text differs between if/else branches is not rebuilt by a general rule; only the Clinic query-specific templates Q014 and Q016 do this.

items.title: Schema Analysis
items.requirement: Database tables, columns, data types, primary keys, foreign keys, and relationships must be identified from the MySQL schema.
items.limitation: Relationships are inferred from declared foreign keys only.

items.title: Query and Column Analysis
items.requirement: The tables and columns used by each recovered query must be identified, as well as how those columns are subsequently used within the application logic.
items.limitation: Column use is identified per SQL statement only; how result columns are used later in the PHP application logic is not traced.

items.title: ORM Generation
items.requirement: The system must generate SQLAlchemy models with appropriate data types, keys, and relationships.
items.limitation: Tables without a primary key become Core Table objects, not ORM classes. A schema-only sqlacodegen comparison (evidence/baseline) was run on all nine apps and found model parity on tables, columns, primary keys, nullability and types; foreign keys could be compared on twelve relationships in four apps only, because the other five apps declare none.

items.title: Data Access Generation
items.requirement: SQL operations that can be safely recovered must be converted into parameterized SQLAlchemy data access functions.
items.limitation: Only static INNER JOIN SELECTs are converted: LEFT JOIN and implicit comma-join sites are recovered but not converted. MySQL behavioural equivalence (E1) exists for HMS only.

items.title: Safety Checking
items.requirement: It must be verified whether runtime values can be safely parameterized, and dynamic values used in structural positions such as table names or column names must be identified.
items.limitation: E4 is a recording-session check with a fixed payload set (no database); runtime hostile testing on MySQL exists for HMS only.

items.title: Safe Abstention
items.requirement: Queries that cannot be migrated confidently or safely must be flagged for human review rather than generating incorrect code.
items.limitation: Correct abstention is measurable only where the ground truth has non-recoverable sites; flagged sites get a reason and a stub, never generated SQL.

items.title: Migration Support
items.requirement: Alembic migration information required for the modernized data layer must be generated.
items.limitation: Initial-schema revision only, no data migration.

items.title: Traceability
items.requirement: The original PHP file and source location must be maintained for each recovered database operation. This information can be used for review and debugging purposes.
items.limitation: Checked by matching every evaluated site on file and line. The frozen HMS signatures.json is identical to the handoff tag (line endings aside), matches its recorded hash, and every php_site label in it is the pipeline's own label; HMS_HANDOFF.md, edited after the tag, cites the Q036 site without its include/ directory and has not been regenerated.
